Analysis.object: This study highlights gender differences in muscle dysmorphia (MD) symptoms among powerlifters, with men showing higher symptom levels and women experiencing greater body-related distress. Self-esteem, social media comparisons, and performance emerge as key associated factors.

The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the small, non-representative sample—particularly among women—reduces generalizability. Potential selection bias and reliance on self-reported data also affect validity.

Future longitudinal and cross-cultural studies with larger samples are needed. Interventions targeting self-esteem, media literacy, and performance-related pressures may help reduce MD risk in athletes.

Population.object: Being at least 18 years old, currently competing in powerlifting competitions and absence of self-reported body image disorder
